caption:
Song stuck in your head and no idea what it's called? Hum it. Google names it.

WHY IT WORKS: Google says a song's melody is like its fingerprint. Its machine-learning models turn your hum into a number pattern of the tune and compare it with thousands of songs, so you don't need the words or perfect pitch.

HOW (about 20 seconds):
1. Open the free Google app (Android or iPhone).
2. Tap the mic in the search bar.
3. Tap "Search a song".
4. Hum, whistle or sing the tune for 10 to 15 seconds.
5. Tap the match that looks right, then play it to check.

THE CATCH: you get possible matches, not a sure answer. Hum the catchiest part, usually the chorus. On iPhone it works in English; on Android it works in more than 20 languages.

PRIVACY TIP: what the mic hears is sent to Google to find the match. Hum somewhere quiet, away from conversations you'd rather keep private.

The phone screen in this Reel is drawn for this post, not a screen recording.

caption:
Phone bill went up and you don't know why? Paste last month's and this month's bill into an AI chat and ask what changed.

WHY IT WORKS: comparing two lists line by line is tedious for you and quick for AI. It answers from what you paste, so it can point to the exact line that changed.

THE REAL TEST: we made up two phone bills (September $100.85, October $117.80). The only real difference: October had no $15 loyalty discount. We asked Claude (Anthropic) on Oct 25, 2026: "Here are my last two phone bills. Why is October's higher? Answer in one short sentence, then list what changed."
Its first line, quoted exactly: "October is $16.95 higher because your $15 loyalty discount went away, and that also raised your tax." It also listed tax going from $11.60 to $13.55 (+$1.95). We checked the maths: both right.

HOW:
1. Open both bills in your provider's app or the PDFs.
2. Copy the line items, or take screenshots.
3. Cover your account number, name, address and phone number.
4. Paste both into ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini and ask: "Why is this month higher? List what changed."
5. Find the line it names on your real bill before you call.

THE CATCH: AI can misread a blurry screenshot or add wrong, so check the line it points to. It can't see your contract: if a discount ended, ask your provider whether it can come back.

PRIVACY TIP: cover your account number, address and phone number before you paste. "My phone bill" is all the AI needs.

caption:
He wants $500. Again. Ask Claude (or ChatGPT or Gemini) to help you say no, and add three words: kind, firm, no excuses.

AI, for real · Day 9. One real test of what AI can do, with the output shown.

WHY IT WORKS: without a tone, AI guesses, and the guess is often long, apologetic or full of reasons. Naming the tone tells it what to aim for. "No excuses" matters most: it stops the AI inventing a reason you'd then have to defend.

THE REAL TEST (the situation is made up for this post):
Request: "My friend wants to borrow $500. He still owes me $200 from last time. Write a short text saying no. Kind, firm, no excuses."
Claude's reply (Claude, by Anthropic, Oct 25, 2026, fresh chat). It wrote two versions, quoted exactly:
1. "Hey, I'm going to pass on this one. I hope it works out, and I'm here if you want to talk it through."
   Its note: "Then bring up the $200 another time. Mixing the two can make the no sound like you're punishing him."
2. "Hey, I'm not able to lend you the $500. I care about you and hope things work out. Also, could you let me know when you'll be able to pay back the $200 from last time?"
Notice: no excuse in either one. Pick the first to keep today's no simple, the second if you want the $200 settled now.

Before you send it, change any word that doesn't sound like you.

PRIVACY TIP: you don't need his name or your bank details. "My friend" and the amount are enough.

Do this: next time a text is hard to write, ask Claude, ChatGPT or Gemini for it and end with "Kind, firm, no excuses."
